source_text: Haec locutus sum caritati uestrae propter illud quod dixistis: aut hic aut nusquam. hoc enim et nos uolumus, ut \'hic hic\' sed in pace, hic hic\' sed in unitate, \'hic hic\' sed in caritatis societate. tunc bene (hi c). nam (si non sic), melius \'nusquam\' quam hic). sed praestet dominus, ut hic) potius quam \'nusquam\'. si non \'hic\', absit ut non alibi, absit. hic aut alibi. audistis, audiuit. quid in eius animo deus egerit, ipse nouit. nos enim aurem forinsecus percutimus, ille nouit intus loqui, ille intus praedicat pacem nec cessat praedicare, si audiatur. aderit misericordia eius adiuuantibus orationibus uestris, ut sit fructuosus labor noster. tamen si hodie communicare noluerit, quamuis fatigari non debeamus, sed instare quantum possumus debeamus, nec sic tamen fatigari debemus. differre possumus, auferre instantiam nostram nec possumus nec debemus. aderit ille qui huc illum ad nos perduxit, ut nos faciat cum illo in unitate uobiscum et in sua pace gaudere.
thought_title: Here or nowhere, but in peace and unity
orientation: Augustine is addressing the congregation at Caesarea, explaining the meaning of their acclamation 'here or nowhere' and expressing hope that Emeritus, who is present, will be won to Catholic unity.
pass_a_gloss: These things I have spoken to [your] charity on account of that which you said: either here or nowhere. this indeed also we wish, that 'here here' but in peace, 'here here' but in unity, 'here here' but in [the] fellowship of charity. then well (here). for (if not thus), better 'nowhere' than here). but may [the] Lord grant, that here) rather than 'nowhere'. if not 'here', far be it that not elsewhere, far be it. here or elsewhere. you heard, he heard. what in his soul God has done, he himself knows. we indeed [the] ear from outside strike, he knows within to speak, he within preaches peace and does not cease to preach, if he is heard. [the] mercy of him will be present [with] [your] helping prayers, that [our] labor may be fruitful. nevertheless if today he is unwilling to communicate, although we ought not to be wearied, but to press on as much as we can we ought, not thus nevertheless to be wearied we ought. to defer we can, to take away our insistence neither we can nor we ought. he will be present who here him to us led, that he may make us with him in unity with you and in his peace to rejoice.

choices.why: Augustine addresses the congregation as 'your love' as a term of address; the glossary requires 'love' for caritas.
This is the congregation's acclamation, kept literal to preserve the force of the slogan.
Societas is rendered 'fellowship' to distinguish it from unitas ('unity') and pax ('peace'), and caritas is 'love' per glossary.

choices.english: far be it that it be not elsewhere, far be it
choices.why: The double absit is emphatic; keeping the repetition preserves the rhetorical force.
rejected: God forbid that it be not elsewhere, God forbid
let it not be that it is not elsewhere

choices.english: we strike the ear from outside
choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the contrast between external preaching and God's internal speech.
rejected: we hit the ear from without

choices.why: In this context it means to enter communion, i.e., to receive the Eucharist in Catholic unity; kept literal as 'communicate' to preserve the technical sense.

pass_b_english: I have said all this to your love because of what you cried out: here or nowhere. For this is what we too want: here, here—but in peace; here, here—but in unity; here, here—but in the fellowship of love. Then here is good. For if it is not so, nowhere is better than here. But may the Lord grant that it be here rather than nowhere. If it is not here, far be it that it be not elsewhere—far be it. Here or elsewhere. You have heard; he has heard. What God has done in his soul, he himself knows. For we strike the ear from outside; he knows how to speak within. He preaches peace within, and he does not cease to preach, if only he will listen. His mercy will be present, with your prayers helping, so that our labor may be fruitful. Yet if he is unwilling to communicate today, although we must not grow weary—but we must press on as much as we can—even so we must not grow weary. We can postpone; we cannot and must not take away our insistence. He who led him here to us will be present, to make us rejoice with him in unity with you and in his peace.

problems.why: si audiatur is passive 'if he is heard,' but context and theology require 'if he listens/hears'—God's inner preaching requires Emeritus's receptive hearing, not others hearing him.
problems.ruling: 'si audiatur' is passive 'if he is heard'; context requires active 'if he hears/listens'—God preaches within.

fixed: Changed 'if only he is heard' to 'if only he will listen' because the source 'si audiatur' is passive but the context requires Emeritus's receptive hearing of God's inner preaching, not others hearing God.

last_rejected.why: Latin is passive 'if he is heard,' not active 'if he will listen.'
last_rejected.ruling: Deponent audio often means 'listen'; 'if he is heard' makes no sense for inward preaching context.

last_rejected.why: Subject is God/He (ille), not 'he' referring to Emeritus; ambiguous English hides agency.
last_rejected.ruling: 'ille' refers to God; English 'He' can match. Not a major error, just capitalization preference.

last_rejected.quote: he knows how to speak within
last_rejected.why: Subject is God (ille), not Emeritus; 'he' is ambiguous and misleading.
last_rejected.fix: He knows how to speak within
last_rejected.ruling: 'ille' = God; 'he' is grammatically correct. Capitalization is stylistic, not a major mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: he knows how to speak within. He preaches peace within
last_rejected.source_quote: ille nouit intus loqui, ille intus praedicat pacem
last_rejected.why: English 'he' twice refers to God, but lowercase and context make it seem like Emeritus.
last_rejected.fix: He knows how to speak within. He preaches peace within
last_rejected.ruling: Pronoun reference is clear from context; capitalization is a stylistic preference, not a major error.
